title: Global self-similar solutions for Hardy-Hénon equations with linear and quasilinear diffusion
summary: Global self-similar solutions to the parabolic Hardy-Hénon equation $$ u_t=Δu^m+|x|^σu^p, \quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^N\times(0,\infty), $$ are classified in the range of exponents $m\geq1$, $p>m$ and $σ>\max\{-2,-N\}$. The classification varies strongly with respect to the celebrated \emph{Fujita} and \emph{Sobolev critical exponents} $$ p_F(σ)=m+\frac{σ+2}{N}, \quad p_S(σ)= \begin{cases} \frac{m(N+2σ+2)}{N-2}, & \mbox{if } N\geq3, \\[1mm] \infty, & \mbox{if } N\in\{1,2\}. \end{cases} $$ Indeed, if $p\in(p_F(σ),p_S(σ))$, both equations admit self-similar solutions with either compact support…
